text:
maria: Hey team — customer hitting weird duplicate requests + AbortError when our TS SDK retries. Node 18.15, @redwood/sdk@1.2.3. They see a request fail with AbortError and then another attempt goes out immediately.
support-bot: New support ticket created: #S-4921 (linked).
alex: Can you paste minimal repro and logs? esp. stack trace and headers (x-request-id, retry-count).
maria: Logs attached (redacted). Main bits: 
```
Error: The operation was aborted
 at fetch (node:internal/fetch)
 at Request.execute (/usr/src/app/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.js:412:22)
 at RetryWrapper.attempt (/usr/src/app/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/retries.js:87:12)
```
Also saw repeated 429s then retries that appear to share the same AbortController signal.
chris: Hmm this sounds like signal reuse across retry attempts. undici/node-fetch will throw if the signal was aborted previously — if the SDK reuses the incoming signal or reuses an AbortController instance across attempts you can get an immediate AbortError on subsequent tries.
jonah: Which undici version is the customer using? there were behavior changes around signals in undici v5.
maria: undici@4.14.2 bundle via node's global fetch (node 18 builtin). SDK uses its internal retry wrapper. Customer code snippet: 
```
const res = await client.chat.completions.create({ prompt }, { signal: controller.signal });
// then client retries internally if 429
```
samir: If they pass their own signal into SDK, SDK must not reuse it for internal per-attempt timeouts. SDK should listen and cancel overall request, but create a fresh AbortController for per-attempt timeouts.
alex: For triage: can you try two quick things with the customer? 1) set retry: { limit: 0 } in SDK options to confirm duplicates stop. 2) upgrade SDK to 1.3.0-rc (has a signal handling patch).
maria: Tested with retry limit 0 — duplicates stop but they then see more 429s and worse latency (makes sense). Tried 1.3.0-rc — reduced incidents but one customer still reports occasional aborts.
chris: Another workaround: when forwarding a user-supplied signal into our client, do not pass it directly to underlying fetch. Instead do: 
```
const overall = userSignal;
for (attempt...) {
  const attemptCtrl = new AbortController();
  const mergedSignal = mergeSignals(overall, attemptCtrl.signal); // small util
  await fetch(url, { signal: mergedSignal });
}
```
If we can't merge, ensure we recreate attempt controller each try and don't re-use the same controller instance.
jonah: Also note Node 18's global fetch uses undici under the hood; their undici version + runtime behavior matters. On Node 20 this is less flaky. Recommend testing on Node 20 if feasible.
maria: I'll ask the customer to test Node 20 and to try SDK 1.3.0-rc with retry policy tuned.
alex: For product/dev: can we add a guard in the SDK to detect if an incoming AbortSignal has been aborted and then fail-fast with a clear message (instead of reusing), and always create internal per-attempt controllers?
chris: Agreed. Patch idea: in request runner, if options.signal is provided, copy it but never pass the original to underlying fetch. Also add unit tests simulating multiple aborts and simulated 429 then success.
maria: I'll collect repro and attach gist. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/support-4921 (private)
deploy-bot: canary rollout 1.3.0-rc -> support group in 2m :rocket:
alex: TL;DR for support: 1) short-term workaround: set retry.limit = 0 or ensure caller doesn't reuse the same AbortController across different logical requests; 2) recommend upgrade to 1.3.0-rc / Node 20; 3) we'll ship SDK patch to always create per-attempt AbortController and merge signals safely. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks — I'll update the customer and paste their results here.
